subject: [RFC PATCH 0/7] cgroup: charge kernel work to the cgroup it is done for

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Peter Zijlstra noted that proxy execution can alleviate the issue, suggesting that tasks waiting on a lock acquisition should contribute to the runnability of the lock holder.

Reviewer Peter Zijlstra strongly disagrees with the patch's approach to charging kernel work to a cgroup, calling it 'horrible garbage' and suggesting that if weight adjustments are needed, using C[23] would be preferable.

Reviewer Peter Zijlstra suggested that instead of moving existing kthreads, new threads should be spawned on cgroup creation and left there, also recommending a less ugly solution to the rmdir issue.
reviews.raw_body:
With proxy execution, this should be alleviated. Then all tasks waiting
on a lock acquisition will contribute to the runnability of the lock
holder.

---

Fiddling with weight sounds like horrible garbage. If you find you need
that, I would really rather you went C[23].

---

You don't move the threads, you spawn them on group creation and leave
them there. I'm sure you can fudge the rmdir thing with less ugly than
you're proposing here and in the other series.

reviews.author: Peter Zijlstra
reviews.summary: Reviewer Peter Zijlstra suggested splitting RX softirqs for each network queue to allow for better resource isolation and priority control, which would enable moving the RX processing threads into specific cgroups.
reviews.raw_body:
Ideally RX would be split for each network queue, rather than lumped
into the one giant softirq that nobody owns.

I know PREEMPT_RT has been wanting something like that for ages. Not all
queues are created equal. Some might want RT priority while others
should definitely not.

Furthermore, without ingress throttling, your RX back charge could
completely deplete the actual cgroup time quota.

Anyway, if you get per queue RX processing threads, then you can move
them into cgroups where so desired.

reviews.author: Sebastian Siewior
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested modifying softirq flags from per-CPU to per-thread, citing threaded NAPI as an example of a working solution and proposing bulk queues and real-time queues as alternatives.
reviews.raw_body:
What currently kind of works is threaded NAPI. The interrupt wakes the
NAPI thread rather than adding NET_RX to the global flag softirq flags.

I was thinking about making the softirq flags per-thread rather than
per-CPU. This avoid the "catch up" of other raised but unrelated
softirqs.

For now a painless setup is to have "bulk queues" and "real-time" queues
and what gets where is configured via hardware filters.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that accurate CPU accounting for net rx in older NICs requires cgroup-aware CPU accounting, agreeing with Peter Zijlstra's feedback.
reviews.raw_body:
For the accurate cpu accounting of net rx, threaded NAPI or softirq is not
that important. I think it is steering packets of the workload/cgroup to their
dedicated queues and only newer NICs have support for hardware rx steering.

For old NICs, we will still be getting packets for different cgroups on the
same NIC queue and I think Tejun is asking for cgroup cpu accounting for this
scenario to work.

reviews.author: Tejun Heo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not address the issue of kworkers running in the root cgroup, which results in inaccurate CPU accounting and pressure metrics for the affected cgroups.

Reviewer noted that splitting RX work per queue does not provide sufficient granularity, as there can be many more cgroups than the hardware can support

Tejun Heo noted that if a kthread is handling RX processing for a cgroup, it would share CPU time with other tasks in the cgroup without starving them, and suggested that back-charging can follow a similar principle.

Reviewer Tejun Heo noted that the patch does not address the issue of CPU contention in setups with many cgroups, and requested further consideration to ensure accurate resource isolation.
reviews.raw_body:
Hello, Peter.

On Thu, Oct 01, 2026 at 12:59:09PM +0200, Peter Zijlstra wrote:

---

Rx can be split per queue but the granularity doesn't match. There can be
way more cgroups than the hardware can split queues for.

---

If rx processing slows down, the rx traffic slows down with it. We'd
likely still want to allot some minimum amount of time to non-rx work
while making sure the debt doesn't spiral out of control. If a dedicated
kthread were handling rx for the cgroup, rx would be sharing CPU time with
the rest of the cgroup without choking it completely. The back charging
can follow the same corollary.

---

Same limit here. There are setups with a lot more cgroups than CPUs.

Thanks.

--
tejun

2026-10-01.patch_summary: This patch series introduces a mechanism to charge kernel work to the cgroup it is being done for, rather than charging it to the root cgroup. This addresses a problem where CPU time spent by kernel threads on behalf of a specific cgroup is not accounted for in that cgroup's statistics and quotas. The approach taken involves allowing kernel threads to specify which cgroup they are working for, and then updating the relevant statistics and quotas accordingly. This will improve resource isolation and accuracy of accounting for CPU usage in various scenarios, including memory reclaim from high-work queues.
